contrary_evidence: The tariff investigation had not produced a formally published duty schedule by the stated cutoff; the reported ceilings may not become adopted rates.
US consumer confidence rose to 103.3 and Q3 GDP advance growth was 3.4% annualized, with real final sales to private domestic purchasers at 4.9%, indicating resilient demand.
European shares rose 0.5% and Brent fell 1% in the cited snapshot while global equities and Asia ex-Japan declined, so the market move was not uniform.
Australian headline CPI includes electricity-rebate/base effects and fuel; trimmed mean at 3.8% is a separate measure, not proof of a purely demand-driven inflation acceleration.
Japan's SPPI excluding international transportation was 3.2%, below the 4.2% all-services measure, showing that freight-related components matter.
The Conference Board confidence index measures survey perceptions and intentions, not realized consumption.
limitations: Tariff ceilings and country exceptions are reported by Reuters from sources familiar with negotiations, not an official USTR determination.
Australia CPI and Japan SPPI have different baskets and transaction stages and are not directly comparable inflation rates.
Conference Board consumer confidence is a survey, not realized household expenditure.
BEA Q3 GDP 3.4% and final-sales 4.9% are the advance-estimate vintage; the second estimate and October PCE were scheduled after the cutoff.
Reuters market snapshots combine Tuesday US closes and early Wednesday regional observations; the article labels observation windows.
No source-audited bilateral trade/finance flow matrix or measured tariff pass-through elasticity is supplied; causal transmission remains conditional.
One of the 11 URLs is a Reuters syndicated reprint and is not counted as independent corroboration.

signal_rationale.delta: The 23 November public edition examined the physical mismatch between Chinese iron-ore imports, steel output, inventories and exporter receipts. The 25 November issue shifts to the transmission of US trade restrictions through import costs, supply-chain decisions, inflation and financing, anchored by fresh Australian CPI and Japanese services-producer data.
signal_rationale.evidence: Reuters reported on 25 November that MSCI global equities fell 0.4% and Asia-Pacific ex-Japan shares fell 3.2% amid imminent findings from a Section 301 investigation into 16 economies. The ABS reported October Australian CPI inflation of 4.9% and trimmed mean of 3.8%. The Bank of Japan reported October services producer-price inflation of 4.2%, or 3.2% excluding international transportation. The Conference Board reported US consumer confidence at 103.3. BEA scheduled October PCE and the Q3 GDP second estimate for 25 November at 8:30 a.m. EST; they were not available by the 07:45 BRT cutoff. Reuters also reported the expected negotiated ceilings: 15% for EU/Japan/South Korea, 19% for Malaysia, a conditional 20% second-term cap for China, and no immediate new levies expected for Mexico and Norway; these were not formally adopted tariff rates at the cut-off.
signal_rationale.scale_path: US trade-policy findings affect product coverage and landed costs; companies adjust suppliers, inventories and investment; changes in import prices, export demand and margins feed into consumer and producer prices; central-bank responses alter yields, exchange rates and cross-border funding conditions.
signal_rationale.transmission: Section 301 findings -> potential tariffs and retaliation -> import prices, sourcing costs and trade diversion -> margins, household prices and investment -> inflation expectations and policy rates -> currencies, yields and financing.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The thesis weakens if the USTR findings produce no material new duties or only narrow measures with broad exemptions, trade volumes and investment plans show no sustained response, US PCE and subsequent services-price data disinflate broadly, and Australian trimmed-mean and Japanese services-price measures return toward prior trajectories.

key_constraints: The Reuters account of imminent USTR findings and expected duties is sourced to people familiar with the matter; as of the 07:45 BRT cutoff, no new tariff schedule had been formally published.
The Section 301 investigation list contains the European Union as a trading bloc; the 16 entries are economies, not 16 individual countries.
The Australian CPI and Japanese SPPI use different baskets and measure different transaction stages; they are not directly comparable inflation rates.
Japan's services producer-price index includes international transportation; the adjusted comparison excludes specified international air, ocean freight, tanker, air-freight and mail services.
US consumer confidence is a survey of perceptions and intentions, not realized household consumption.
The US Q3 GDP advance estimate and the October PCE series are different releases; the second estimate and PCE were scheduled for after the cut-off.
Market figures in the Reuters 25 November report mix Tuesday US closes and early Wednesday regional snapshots; observation windows are labelled separately.
No new tariff rate, product coverage, exemption, implementation date or retaliation has been assumed.
Partner-level caps and country exceptions are attributed to Reuters sources and remain reported expectations; they are not a published USTR tariff schedule.
